STEP 1 - Scene: A single whole apple on a white plate, photographed from directly overhead.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square-ish white plate. Its width is about 350 px in the image. The apple is about 128 px wide, so if the plate is ~24 cm across (roughly 350 px), the apple is about 8.7 cm across. That looks too large for a typical apple, so the plate is more likely ~22 cm, which gives an apple of ~8 cm. The plate area is about 22² ≈ 480 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: One red/yellow apple (no other food visible).

STEP 4 - Area: The apple's footprint is a circle with ~8 cm diameter, so about 50 cm², or ~10% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: An apple is roughly a sphere with an 8 cm diameter. Volume = 4/3 × 3.14 × 4³ ≈ 268 ml. Apples are slightly flattened, so I take ~250 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole-apple density is ~0.85 g/ml, so 250 × 0.85 ≈ 210 g. This is a medium apple including the core, which fits.

STEP 7 - Energy: Apple is about 52 kcal/100 g, so 210 g gives ~109 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A medium apple weighs 180–220 g and has ~95–110 kcal, so the estimate is plausible.
